entries.content_plain: CHAPTER (ELEGY) 2 La 2:1-22 . Aleph. 1. How-- The title of the collection repeated here, and in La 4:1 . covered ... with a cloud-- that is, with the darkness of ignominy. cast down from heaven unto ... earth-- ( Mt 11:23 ); dashed down from the highest prosperity to the lowest misery. beauty of Israel-- the beautiful temple ( Psa 29:2 ; 74:7 ; 96:9 , Margin; Is 60:7 ; 64:11 ). his footstool-- the ark (compare 1Ch 28:2 , with Psa 99:5 ; 132:7 ). They once had gloried more in the ark than in the God whose symbol it was; they now feel it was but His "footstool," yet that it had been a great glory to them that God deigned to use it as such. Beth.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10823"/><div sID="gen19451" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10823"/><hi type="bold">13. What thing shall I take to witness--</hi>What can I bring forward as a witness, or instance, to prove that others have sustained as grievous ills as thou? I cannot console thee as mourners are often consoled by showing that thy lot is only what others, too, suffer. The "sea" affords the only suitable emblem of thy woes, by its boundless extent and depth (<reference osisRef="Lam.1.12">La 1:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.9.12">Da 9:12</reference>).<div eID="gen19451" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19452" type="x-p"/> Nun. <div eID="gen19452" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10824"/><div sID="gen19453" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10824"/><hi type="bold">14. Thy prophets--</hi>not God's (<reference osisRef="Jer.23.26">Jr 23:26</reference>).<div eID="gen19453" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19454" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">vain ... for thee--</hi>to gratify thy appetite, not for truth, but for false things.<div eID="gen19454" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19455" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">not discovered thine iniquity--</hi>in opposition to God's command to the true prophets (<reference osisRef="Isa.58.1">Is 58:1</reference>). Literally, "They have not taken off (the veil) which was on thine iniquity, so as to set it before thee."<div eID="gen19455" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19456" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">burdens--</hi>Their prophecies were soothing and flattering; but the result of them was heavy calamities to the people, worse than even what the prophecies of Jeremiah, which they in derision called "burdens," threatened. Hence he terms their pretended prophecies "false burdens," which proved to the Jews "causes of their banishment" [Calvin].<div eID="gen19456" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen19457" type="x-p"/> Samech. <div eID="gen19457" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 14. Thy prophets-- not God's ( Jr 23:26 ). vain ... for thee-- to gratify thy appetite, not for truth, but for false things. not discovered thine iniquity-- in opposition to God's command to the true prophets ( Is 58:1 ). Literally, "They have not taken off (the veil) which was on thine iniquity, so as to set it before thee." burdens-- Their prophecies were soothing and flattering; but the result of them was heavy calamities to the people, worse than even what the prophecies of Jeremiah, which they in derision called "burdens," threatened. Hence he terms their pretended prophecies "false burdens," which proved to the Jews "causes of their banishment" [Calvin]. Samech.

Thy prophets-- not God's ( Jr 23:26 ). vain ... for thee-- to gratify thy appetite, not for truth, but for false things. not discovered thine iniquity-- in opposition to God's command to the true prophets ( Is 58:1 ). Literally, "They have not taken off (the veil) which was on thine iniquity, so as to set it before thee." burdens-- Their prophecies were soothing and flattering; but the result of them was heavy calamities to the people, worse than even what the prophecies of Jeremiah, which they in derision called "burdens," threatened. Hence he terms their pretended prophecies "false burdens," which proved to the Jews "causes of their banishment" [Calvin]. Samech.
